text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 7.2% today, following a sharp drop of more than $33 from its October 20 peak. The primary driver is the sudden shift in oil market sentiment: overnight, Iran's supreme leader and top security officials began discussing conditions to end the regional war, which sparked a sell-off in crude prices. Lower oil prices directly squeeze refiner margins—the profit refiners make by converting crude into fuel—since they sell gasoline and diesel at prices that don't fall as fast as crude does.

The timing matters: just two days ago, the stock had bounced to $470 on Middle East escalation fears that pushed Brent crude to a six-month high above $116. Now that geopolitical risk is unwinding, traders are repricing the refiner's earnings outlook downward. Refinery utilization is still solid at 93.4%, but the profit environment has deteriorated sharply in 48 hours as the market has shifted from betting on supply disruption to betting on a diplomatic resolution.
